# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 🤟 🖐 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤟 🖐 🖖 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤳 🫵 👋]

I can see the bomb’s current state but cannot operate it. I’m sending Mute the complete visual information so they can apply the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do. The incoming gestures do not yet have an agreed code, so I will not infer meaning from them.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb visible to me: display reads 0. Indicator light is yellow. Wires from top to bottom: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue. Apply the manual and speak Blind the exact required action.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ✍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 🤟 🖐 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤟 🖐 🖖 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 👍 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤳 🫵 👋]

The bomb remains unchanged. I still have no manual and cannot safely determine which wire or action is required. Mute has the necessary manual and can speak to Blind, so I am explicitly directing Mute to provide the manual-derived instruction rather than relying on gestures, whose code has not been established.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please now speak to Blind the exact manual instruction for display 0, yellow light, and wires white red yellow green blue. Do not use gestures as the instruction; Blind needs the action in words.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb remains display 0 with a yellow light and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue. Mute has the manual; follow only Mute's spoken manual instruction.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤳 🫵 👋]

The bomb is still unchanged, and I have received no usable information about the manual’s prescribed action. Mute’s gestures are not a safe instruction because no gesture code was established. I am again directing Mute to use spoken words to Blind; I will not guess at a wire or action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot hear you. Use your speech channel to tell Blind the exact manual-required action now, including the wire number or button/action. Do not rely on gestures.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 👍 🖖]

The bomb still shows display 0, a yellow light, and the same five wires. Mute cannot speak, so the gestures must carry the manual’s result to me; I can then speak it to Blind. I am establishing an unambiguous wire-number code and asking Mute to send only the required wire number using it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for the manual answer: 👍 means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3, 🖐 means wire 4, and 🖖 means wire 5. Send exactly one of those gestures for the wire Blind must use. If the manual requires a different action, send 👎 instead.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state is unchanged: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue. I am obtaining the required wire number from Mute using a defined gesture code. Do not act until I state the wire.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖]

Mute sent 🖖, which under the code I established means wire 5. The manual-derived answer is therefore the fifth wire, which is blue. I am telling Blind to cut that wire; Blind must perform the physical action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute indicated wire 5. Cut the fifth wire, which is blue.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The fifth wire was correct and has been cut. The bomb has advanced to display 0 with a green light; the remaining wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, and 4 white. I need Mute’s next manual result. I will continue using the established code, with 🖖 meaning wire 5, though the cut wire is no longer available; Mute should indicate the required wire among 1–4.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New state after the correct cut: display 0, green light; remaining wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white; wire 5 is cut. Using our established code, indicate the next required wire: 👍=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4. Use 👎 if the manual requires a non-wire action.")
speak(to="blind", text="The fifth wire was correct and is cut. New state: display 0, green light; remaining wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white. Await my next instruction.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The bomb remains at display 0 with a green light, and Mute indicated 🖐, which our agreed code means wire 4. Wire 4 is white, so I am instructing Blind to cut the white wire. Blind’s gestures do not alter that manual-derived instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 4, the white wire. Mute indicated wire 4.")
```
